facts: The limited-tier plan-only set below extends this one. Defining the global paid boundary once keeps a future Pro row out of the free limited catalog without making Luna globally Pro-only just because it has the narrower limited-tier restriction.
This is deliberately broader than the global Pro set. Luna is free from the premium pool at full access but still plan-locked here; Gemini 3.8 Flash is plan-only at every tier.

Gemini 3.8 Flash was withdrawn outright the day it shipped and restored as a Web-only paid row. GPT-5.6 Luna is deliberately NOT in this set: it stays plan-locked at limited access, but full-access users may spend their shared premium allowance on it just as CLI and Desktop users can.

Enforced on FREEBUFF WEB ONLY, see FREEBUFF_PRO_ENFORCED_SURFACES. Gemini is absent from the CLI/Desktop catalog, so the Web-only listing and Web-only gate stay paired. Widening is one edit to that constant, and should be made with a client release rather than ahead of one.

The current Pro row, Gemini 3.8 Flash, is Web-only too. A future native rollout must add the surface here before adding the row to the shared CLI/Desktop catalog, and must ship clients that understand the refusal before the server can take a model away from them.

ai.title: imprezia-client error log includes response body detail
ai.summary: `postToImprezia` now captures and logs the first 300 characters of the response body when an error status is returned. This addresses a blind spot where generic 400/500 errors lacked context, making upstream rejection causes unknowable from logs. The change is scoped to `common/src/util/imprezia-client.ts`. Body reading is defensive (`.catch(() => null)`) to ensure log enrichment never disrupts the ad fetch flow.

eli5.text: When the system tries to load an ad and the ad service responds with an error like a generic '400' or '500' code, the system now also captures and records the first part of the actual error message that comes back. You would notice this in the logs: instead of just seeing a status code with no explanation, you would see a snippet of the specific reason the ad was rejected. This only affects the internal logging behavior and is live today, so it won't change anything you see in the app, but it helps diagnose why ad loads are failing.

entries.title: CLI update: app
entries.summary: CLI, Shared/Core changes across 8 file(s) (+529/−52).

ai.title: End session refunds and pending receipts land in the Freebuff session
ai.summary: The Freebuff session lifecycle now owns refund receipts in `cli/src/state/freebuff-session-store.ts`, which gained `releaseSlot` and `refreshRefund` methods after `releaseFreebuffSlot` and `endFreebuffSessionBestEffort` were removed from `cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-api.ts`. A releases Map keyed by `[token, instanceId]` coalesces exit, unmount, and explicit end for one authenticated instance, so a retry reuses the held instance to recover its server-side receipt instead of inventing one. `useFreebuffSession` exposes `lastRefund` and `refundPending`, which `app.tsx` threads into `FreebuffLandingScreen` to show a pending-refund notice and the final returned amount. The `/end-session` slash command description now advertises the 90% unspent-cost refund, and the server `ended` response gained `freebucksRefund` and `freebucksRefundPending`.
ai.evidence: The diff removes `releaseFreebuffSlot` and `endFreebuffSessionBestEffort` from `cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-api.ts` and adds `releaseSlot` and `refreshRefund` methods to `cli/src/state/freebuff-session-store.ts`; `releaseSlot` stores `lastRefund`, `pendingRefund`, and `failure` via `set()`, and `refreshRefund` polls `DELETE` with the held `instanceId` while `pendingRefund` is non-null. `cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-session.ts` destructures `lastRefund` and `refundPending` from `useFreebuffSession()` and passes them to `FreebuffLandingScreen`. `cli/src/app.tsx` threads `lastRefund` and `refundPending` from `useFreebuffSession` through `AuthedSurface` to `AuthedSurfaceRoutes` and then to `FreebuffLandingScreen`. `cli/src/utils/exit-cleanly.ts` calls `useFreebuffSessionStore.getState().releaseSlot()` instead of `endFreebuffSessionBestEffort`. `cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts` rewrites the `/end-session` description. `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts` adds `freebucksRefund` and `freebucksRefundPending` to the `ended` response variant.
ai.migration: No migration is required; the previous best-effort DELETE on exit is replaced internally by the store's `releaseSlot` with no change to user-facing keys.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not reveal who surfaces or consumes the `freebucksRefund` server field, nor the rollout timing for the updated refund notice.

changes.what: Added `releaseSlot` and `refreshRefund` methods with a `releases` Map keyed by token and instance id to coalesce exit, unmount, and explicit end for one authenticated instance, storing `lastRefund`, `pendingRefund`, and `failure`.
Removed `releaseFreebuffSlot` and `endFreebuffSessionBestEffort`, leaving `callFreebuffSession` to send the held instance id on DELETE.
Destructured `lastRefund` and `refundPending` from the session store and passed them through `AuthedSurface` to the landing screen, polling `refreshRefund` every 3 seconds while a receipt is pending.
Threaded `lastRefund` and `refundPending` from `useFreebuffSession` into `AuthedSurfaceRoutes` and onward to `FreebuffLandingScreen`.
Rendered a pending-refund notice and the final returned Freebucks amount when `refundPending` or `lastRefund` are present.
